svg.title: Identity and access in the landing zone: who, where identities live, how sign-in is protected, and what they can do
svg.desc: Four columns from left to right. 1, who needs access: employees, administrators with separate cloud-only accounts, external users through Microsoft Entra B2B, and applications using managed identities. 2, where identities live: Microsoft Entra ID, with cloud-only accounts or accounts synchronized from on-premises Active Directory by Microsoft Entra Connect or Cloud Sync; and an identity platform subscription with Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain controllers or Microsoft Entra Domain Services, only for applications that need Kerberos or NTLM. 3, protect sign-in and privileged access: multifactor authentication, Conditional Access, Privileged Identity Management and emergency access accounts. 4, what they can do: Azure role-based access control, with a role assigned to a group at a scope, from management group to subscription to resource group. Footer notes: Microsoft Entra ID roles manage the directory while Azure RBAC roles manage Azure resources, and Azure Policy is assigned at the management group. Icons are official: Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Entra Domain Services, Management groups, Subscriptions and Resource groups.
svg.text: Identity and access in the landing zone
A role, given to a group,
Microsoft Entra ID roles manage the directory and
tenant-wide services. Azure RBAC roles manage Azure
resources such as subscriptions and virtual machines.
Policy is assigned at the management group, so landing
zone administrators with roles at a lower scope cannot
change the policies that govern them.
